rows are written once by the closing run and never corrected afterwards — a

why the clock is handed in rather than read here.

module_docstring: Core package: ports, configuration and error types shared by all contexts.

Adapter facade.

The only module that reaches into ``depot.core.adapters.internal``. Context
services take the session, the cache and the port protocols from here; the
public storage adapter next door they import directly.

The re-exports resolve lazily. Depot code imports whole modules
(``import depot.x.y``) and never single names, so a name of a sub-package
cannot be read while this package is still executing — at that moment
``depot.core`` does not carry the ``adapters`` attribute yet. Resolving on
first attribute access sidesteps that without giving up the import style.

This is the surface the context services depend on. It keeps the documents that
belong to a parcel — the shipping label, the customs form, the handover
manifest — and it is deliberately free of any database session: the facade owns
those.

It is also free of a clock. The day a document is filed under comes in with the
document, because the shift that produced a manifest and the moment it reaches
the store are not the same thing.

module_docstring:
Read models behind the counter overview screen.

The clerk at the counter needs one flat row per customer — name, how much is
waiting on the shelf, when they were last here. No single table holds that, and
joining it per keystroke was too slow on the depot's hardware, so a nightly job
writes these rows and the screen reads them straight. They are never written
